Subject: Recap + next steps: deployment path and pricing comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

Thanks Emily & Tom — great discussion today. Quick recap and the asks we promised to follow up on: 

1) Goals we heard
- Primary: embed LLM-powered content-ranking and short-response generation into your customer support app with sub-200ms 99th percentile for single-turn queries.
- Secondary: occasional batch embedding runs for content search indexing (daily).
- Compliance: EU & US data residency for user content; SOC2-equivalent logs and audit for customer 1 (pilot).

2) Clarifying questions we need to model economics accurately (can you confirm by EOD Wed?):
- Expected steady-state qps (user-facing queries / sec) and peak qps? You mentioned ~60 qps average, ~220 peak — please confirm.
- Average prompt + response token mix (approx. 40 tokens in, 120 tokens out per request?)
- % of requests that require retrieval/context (i.e., longer sequences / KV cache hits) vs plain responses
- Preferred deployment mode if security/legal requires it (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved pool vs Private VPC/on-prem)
- Committed term you would consider for reserved capacity (12 / 24 months) and any target invoice cadence for finance (monthly / quarterly)

3) What we’ll send you today (attachments):
- BRIGHTBRIDGE-workload-snapshot.xlsx — fill-in snapshot we discussed; please add exact QPS and token mix.
- A concise cost comparison: Hosted API (pay-per-token), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), Private VPC (one-time on-prem estimate + infra run-rate). Assumptions and sensitivity bands included.

4) Proposed immediate next steps
- You: confirm the workload numbers and residency constraints (reply inline).
- Us: send a short cost model + recommended pilot configuration and a proposed MA (mutual action) plan for a 6-week pilot.
- If Dedicated or VPC looks like the right fit, we’ll include a sample reserved commit sketch and a draft SOW for legal.

Attachments: BRIGHTBRIDGE-workload-snapshot.xlsx (attachment)

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor

Hi Grace,

Thanks — quick answers inline:
- QPS: confirm ~60 qps steady-state; spikes to ~220 qps during our weekly digest window (10-15 minutes).
- Token mix: average user request ~35 tokens in / 110 tokens out. Longer retrieval flows (10% of traffic) average ~600 tokens out due to context.
- Retrieval/cache: roughly 90% simple responses (KV cache hits), 10% retrieval-heavy.
- Residency: must keep EU-origin data for EU customers in EU region; US customers in the US. For pilot, we can keep all telemetry in US but user input stored EU for EU users if you support a regional deployment.
- Commit term: procurement prefers 12 months, but open to 24 months for a discount. Invoice cadence: monthly preferred.

Attaching a traffic sample we pulled: traffic-sample.csv (attachment).

Regarding preference, security is leaning toward Dedicated reserved capacity if the economics make sense; procurement will need a clear per-user/month or per-1M token equivalent so they can compare to existing vendor spend.

Subject: RE: Recap + next steps: deployment path and pricing comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)

Emily — thanks for the fast answers and the sample. Attached is a short cost rundown (redwood-cost-model-v2.pdf) and the assumptions CSV (econ-assumptions.csv). Highlighted conclusions here so you can share with procurement: 

Assumptions (short):
- Baseline model: 35 in / 110 out tokens per interactive request; retrieval-heavy: 600 tokens out (10% of traffic).
- Region split: 65% US, 35% EU.
- Steady-state qps: 60; peak short window 220.
- Typical reserved GPU profile used for Dedicated: 8xA100-equivalent nodes in a shared pool (blended hourly).

Summary economics (monthly normalized):
- Hosted API (pay-per-token):~ $19,000/month
  - Assumes standard pay-per-token rates and modest caching (30% effective token reduction from caching).
  - Upside: no infra commitment; fastest start.

- Dedicated reserved capacity (12-month commit):~ $12,400/month effective
  - Assumes a 12-month reserved commit for a dedicated GPU pool; includes 20% buffer for bursts.
  - Break-even vs Hosted at ~450M input+output tokens/month.
  - Pros: predictable unit economics, regional pinning possible; Cons: commit + lead time.

- Private VPC / On-prem (one-time infra + run-rate):~ $95k initial + $8k/mo run-rate (ops + infra)
  - Best for customers with strict data locality + long-term cost certainty; higher up-front and internal ops burden.

Pilot recommendation (low friction):
1) 6-week Hosted pilot to validate latency and quality with regional routing for EU traffic; Redwood provides usage dashboard and logs.
2) Parallel reserved-capacity sketch: if procurement confirms a 12-mo commit appetite, we prepare a dedicated pool sketch with final pricing and SOW.

Next actions I’ll take:
- Share the attached PDF + assumptions (done).
- Draft a short pilot mutual action plan by Mon morning.
- If you want, I’ll produce a per-1M-token equivalent number for each option to make procurement comparisons explicit.

Would you like the per-1M-token equivalents in the next doc or shall I include them in the pilot MA?

Attachments: redwood-cost-model-v2.pdf, econ-assumptions.csv

Thanks — Grace
